title: Help the pressed centre-back
brief: Your centre-back plays the ball across the back, and their #9 chases it.
briefKid: Your defender passes across the back, and their striker chases the ball.
question: Your centre-back is under pressure. Where do you go?
questionKid: Their striker is chasing your defender. Where do you go to help?

takeaway.standard: When a teammate is pressed, come short to 5-10 m at an angle with a clear lane, so they have a safe pass out of trouble.
takeaway.kid: Teammate in trouble? Come close so they can pass to you.

misconceptions.text: You stayed where the ball was a moment ago, so your pressed centre-back has no short pass and has to kick it long.
misconceptions.textKid: You stayed where the ball was. Follow it and help your teammate.

misconceptions.text: You hid behind their #9: as they close your centre-back down, they block the pass to you too, so step out of their shadow into a clear lane.
misconceptions.textKid: Their striker is in the way. Move so the pass can reach you.

notes: Their #9 is keyed on a curved pressing run that arrives about 3.5 m from the centre-back, in front and a little inside, at the freeze (pressureOnBall is tagged true from the reception). Left automatic, the #9 was still 6 m off the ball, so the engine's answer stood in the #9's back, 1.75 m off their line to the ball, and spots squarely in the #9's shadow scored S. Now the answer is short and inside the #9 (the #9 is 1.7 m off that pass, early in it), no spot deep in the #9's shadow (lane-open 0.3 or less) scores S, and the shadow region sits on the line from the ball through the #9 and holds no S spot. Engine note: lane-open clears a lane at 1.5 m even for a presser running at the ball and gives partial credit near it, so spots at the edge of the shadow can still score S with the cover-shadow reason.
